summary: From when in the winter do we start saying "mashiv haruach umorid hageshem" in Shemoneh Esrei? Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argue about it.

chunks.en: From when do we mention the power of rain?
chunks.explain: We praise Hashem who "makes the wind blow and the rain fall" in Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: From when, i.e., from which date, does one begin to mention the might of the rains
chunks.stMore: by inserting the phrase: He makes the wind blow and rain fall, in the second blessing of the Amida prayer?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: from the first Yom Tov day of Sukkos.
chunks.st: The phrase is inserted from the first Festival day of the festival of Sukkot.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: from the last Yom Tov day of Sukkos.
chunks.st: From the last Festival day of the festival of Sukkot.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz says "the last Festival day"; Bartenura explains it is Shemini Atzeres.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer:

chunks.en: "Since rain is nothing but
chunks.st: Since rain is nothing other than

chunks.en: a sign of a curse on Sukkos,
chunks.explain: Rain makes us leave the sukkah.
chunks.st: a sign of a curse during the festival of Sukkot,
chunks.stMore: as rainfall forces Jews to leave their sukkot,

chunks.en: why should one mention it?"
chunks.st: why should one mention the might of rain during this period?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:

chunks.en: "I too did not say to ask for rain,
chunks.st: I too did not say that it is proper to request rain at this time,

chunks.en: only to mention 'He makes the wind blow
chunks.st: but it is proper only to mention the phrase: He makes the wind blow

chunks.en: and the rain fall' in its right time."
chunks.st: and rain fall, in its due time.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: "If so,
chunks.st: If so,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if reciting the phrase does not constitute a request for rain,

chunks.en: one should always mention it!"
chunks.st: one should always mention rain, even in the summer.

summary: We ask Hashem for rain only close to the rainy season. This mishnah teaches at which davening we start and stop mentioning rain, and until when we ask for it.
stIntro: The mishna states a general principle:

chunks.en: We do not ask for rain
chunks.st: One requests rain only immediately

chunks.en: except close to the rainy season.
chunks.st: preceding the rainy season.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: the one who leads the davening on the last

chunks.en: Yom Tov of Sukkos (Shemini Atzeres):
chunks.st: concluding Festival day of the festival of Sukkot, the Eighth Day of Assembly:

chunks.en: the last one mentions rain,
chunks.st: The last prayer leader, who leads the additional prayer, mentions rain, whereas

chunks.en: the first one does not mention it.
chunks.st: the first prayer leader, for the morning prayer, does not mention rain.

chunks.en: On the first Yom Tov day of Pesach,
chunks.st: The opposite is the case at the conclusion of the period for mentioning rain on the first Festival day of Passover: Here,

chunks.en: the first one mentions rain,
chunks.st: the first prayer leader, who leads the morning prayer, mentions rain, while

chunks.en: the last one does not mention it.
chunks.st: the last prayer leader, who leads the additional prayer, does not mention rain.

chunks.en: Until when do we ask for rain?
chunks.st: Until when does one request rain?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: We request rain

chunks.en: until Pesach has passed.
chunks.st: until Passover has passed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until Nisan is over,
chunks.st: Until the month of Nisan has ended,

chunks.en: as it says (Yoel 2), "And He brings down rain for you,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And He causes to come down for you the rain, the

chunks.en: the early rain and the late rain, in the first month."
chunks.explain: Nisan is the first month, so it is still rain time.
chunks.st: first rain and the last rain, in the first month” (Joel 2:23).
chunks.stMore: Since the verse states that it rains in Nisan, the first month, this indicates that the entire month is considered part of the rainy season.

summary: On which day in Cheshvan do we begin asking for rain in Shemoneh Esrei? Rabban Gamliel waits a little longer, so the people going home from Yerushalayim stay dry.

chunks.en: On the third of Cheshvan we start asking for rain.
chunks.explain: We add "v'sein tal umatar" in Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: On the third of the month of Marḥeshvan one starts to request rain
chunks.stMore: by inserting the phrase: And give dew and rain, in the blessing of the years, the ninth blessing of the Amida.

words.note: The month after Tishrei, also called Cheshvan.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says: One starts to request rain

A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: on the seventh of it,
chunks.st: on the seventh of Marḥeshvan, which is

chunks.en: fifteen days after Sukkos,
chunks.st: fifteen days after the festival of Sukkot.
chunks.stMore: Rabban Gamliel explains that one waits these extra four days

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ אַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִנְהַר פְּרָת:
chunks.en: so that the last Jew can reach the river Pras.
chunks.explain: People who came to Yerushalayim for Yom Tov need time to walk home dry.
chunks.st: so that the last pilgrim of the Jewish people, who traveled to Jerusalem on foot for the Festival, can reach the Euphrates River
chunks.stMore: without being inconvenienced by rain on his journey home.

words.note: The Euphrates, a big river far from Eretz Yisrael.

summary: If the rain still has not come by the 17th of Cheshvan, some special people start to fast. These fasts are easy ones.

chunks.en: If the 17th of Cheshvan came
chunks.st: If the seventeenth of Marḥeshvan arrived

chunks.en: and no rain has fallen,
chunks.st: and rain has not fallen,

chunks.en: some single people start to fast three fasts.
chunks.explain: Some special people, not the whole community.
chunks.st: individuals, but not the entire community, begin to fast three fasts for rain.

chunks.en: They eat and drink after dark,
chunks.explain: The fast starts only in the morning.
chunks.st: How are these fasts conducted? As the fast begins in the morning, one may eat and drink after dark,

chunks.en: and they may work, wash, put on oil,
chunks.st: and one is permitted during the days of the fasts themselves to engage in the performance of work, in bathing, in smearing oil on one’s body,

chunks.en: wear shoes, and be together as husband and wife.
chunks.st: in wearing shoes, and in conjugal relations.

summary: If the rain still has not come by Rosh Chodesh Kislev, the beis din makes the whole community fast three easy fasts.

chunks.en: If Rosh Chodesh Kislev came
chunks.st: If the New Moon of Kislev arrived

words.note: The first day of a new month.

chunks.en: and no rain has fallen,
chunks.st: and rain has still not fallen, the

chunks.en: the beis din declares three
chunks.st: court decrees three

chunks.en: fasts on the whole community.
chunks.st: fasts on the entire community.
chunks.stMore: Similar to the individual fasts, everyone

chunks.en: They eat and drink after dark,
chunks.st: may eat and drink after dark,

chunks.en: and they may work, wash, put on oil,
chunks.st: and they are permitted to engage in the performance of work, in bathing, in smearing one’s body with oil,

chunks.en: wear shoes, and be together as husband and wife.
chunks.st: in wearing shoes, and in conjugal relations.

summary: If there is still no rain, the beis din makes harder fasts, and then seven more fasts that are even stricter, with stores closed.

chunks.en: If these passed and they were not answered,
chunks.st: If these three regular fasts have passed and they have not been answered with rain, the

chunks.en: the beis din declares three
chunks.st: court decrees three

chunks.en: more fasts on the whole community.
chunks.st: other fasts upon the community.

chunks.en: They eat and drink only while it is still day,
chunks.explain: They stop eating before night, so the fast is a whole day long.
chunks.st: These are severe fasts, in which one may eat and drink only while it is still day,
chunks.stMore: before the beginning of the night of the fast,

chunks.en: and they may not work, wash, put on oil,
chunks.st: and on the day of the fast itself they are prohibited to engage in the performance of work, in bathing, in smearing with oil,

chunks.en: wear shoes, or be together as husband and wife,
chunks.st: in wearing shoes, and in marital relations;

chunks.en: and they lock the bathhouses.
chunks.st: and they lock the bathhouses
chunks.stMore: so that no one should come to bathe on that day.

chunks.en: If these passed and they were not answered,
chunks.st: If these three fasts have passed and they still have not been answered, the

chunks.he: בֵּית דִּין גּוֹזְרִין עֲלֵיהֶם עוֹד שֶׁבַע,
chunks.en: the beis din declares seven more on them,
chunks.st: court decrees on them another seven fasts,

chunks.he: שֶׁהֵן שְׁלשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר.
chunks.en: which makes thirteen fasts on the community.
chunks.st: which are a total of thirteen fasts, upon the community,
chunks.stMore: not including the first three fasts observed by individuals.

chunks.en: These are stricter than the first ones,
chunks.st: These seven fast days are more severe than the first ones,

chunks.en: because on these they sound the alarm and lock the stores.
chunks.explain: They blow the shofar and cry out to Hashem.
chunks.st: as on these days, in addition to all the earlier stringencies, they sound the alarm, as will be explained in the Gemara, and they lock the stores.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains that the alarm means blowing the shofar.

chunks.en: On Monday they open them a little when it gets dark,
chunks.explain: So people can buy food to eat after the fast.
chunks.st: Although shops must remained closed most of the time on these days, on Monday they open them a little at nightfall to allow people to purchase food for breaking their fast,

chunks.en: and on Thursday they are allowed, in honor of Shabbos.
chunks.explain: The stores may stay open so people can buy food for Shabbos.
chunks.st: and on Thursday they are permitted to open the stores all day in deference to Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: so that people may purchase food for the sacred day.

summary: If there is still no rain, everyone acts sad, like people Hashem is upset with. If Nisan ends without rain, it is a sign of a curse.
